items.title: A Brief, Informal History of SFBT as Told by Steve De Shazer and Insoo Kim Berg
items.rights_note: Authorized repository PDF reconstructed from De Jong's notes and interview; explicitly an informal participant account, not rigorous independent historiography.

items.title: Keys to Solution in Brief Therapy
items.rights_note: Open Library bibliographic page for the 1985 first edition; preview status does not authorize caching or treating the book body as read.

items.title: Solution Focused Therapy Treatment Manual for Working with Individuals, Third Edition
items.rights_note: Current SFBTA manual defining framework, techniques and research use; association-authored practice standard, not independent efficacy evidence.

items.title: Examining the effectiveness of solution-focused brief therapy: a meta-analysis
items.rights_note: NCBI Bookshelf mirror of a CRD-DARE critical abstract evaluating Kim's 2008 meta-analysis; it identifies single-reviewer bias, study quality and heterogeneity limitations without standing in for the reviewed article body.
items.failure_note: The newer CRD record was also screened but its direct host failed local TLS verification; this official NCBI Bookshelf DARE mirror was selected instead without disabling certificate checks.

items.title: Effectiveness of solution-focused brief therapy: An umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses
items.rights_note: PubMed abstract and bibliographic record for an umbrella review of 25 systematic reviews; the publisher PDF returned HTTP 403 to the collector, so this is not a full-text read. High overlap and outcome-specific confidence remain boundaries, and absence of consistent harm evidence is not a dedicated safety guideline.
items.failure_note: Open publisher full text was discoverable but its PDF endpoint returned HTTP 403 to the collector; PubMed's official abstract record was retained without bypassing access controls.

items.title: Effectiveness of solution-focused brief therapy on cancer patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.rights_note: CC BY condition-specific meta-analysis of nursing interventions based on SFBT in cancer populations; low certainty, high heterogeneity and risk-of-bias findings prevent general efficacy conclusions.
items.failure_note: The broader 2024 UvA repository meta-analysis was preferred initially but timed out twice at the collector's fixed 60-second limit; this current open condition-specific review was selected without changing retrieval safeguards.

items.title: Meta-Analysis of Solution-Focused Brief Therapy Research Conducted in Iran: Does Outcome Type, Intervention Modality, or Delivery Format Make a Difference?
items.rights_note: CC BY Iran-focused meta-analysis. Regional study designs and outcomes cannot be generalized beyond the Iranian evidence base; its English-publication restriction also means it does not represent the Persian-language corpus.

items.title: Solution Focused Brief Therapy Association
items.rights_note: Current association self-description, manuals, research activity and events; evidence of institutional continuation only.
